headline: Index panic drained but the plumbing didn't: VIX back to 28 while HY widened another 9bp, and the money leaving silicon is going into biotech and the checkout aisle.
summary: What changed overnight is the tone, not the tension. The VIX is 28.29 after printing 34 yesterday, VIX3M 26.29, and the risk regime improved to -19 from -22 with credit & vol at -57 from -66. The index itself barely moved: SPX -0.3% to 7,182.8, and underneath it RUT +0.7%, DJI +0.3%, DJT +1.7%. But the pipes are unhealed. HY OAS went out another 9bp to 3.72 (1m z=1.14, 97th percentile of the year, +102bp in three months), IG 0.98 and BBB 1.22 are both pinned at the 100th percentile, CCC is 14.05 and +520bp YTD. HYG/IEF carries a 1m z of -1.04 and is rolling over. VIX/VIX3M at 1.0761 is still inverted, turning up, with VIX3M acceleration z=0.80 — hedge demand is migrating out the curve, which is what you see before a second leg, not after a washout.

The liquidation is now concentrated and violent in one place: semiconductors. SOXX -8.3%, SMH -7.3% on the session and -19.1% on the month, 18.7% below its 200-day, SMH/SPY z=-2.34. MU -11.0%, AMD -8.9%, NVDA -5.9% to 155.38 (-26.3% in a month), TSM -4.0%, ASML -3.4%, AVGO -4.0%. Asia followed overnight — KOSPI -5.0%, TAIEX -3.2%, EWT -4.1%, EWY -3.7%. The adjacency is cracking with it: GEV -4.8%, ETN -5.1%, VST -2.5%, NLR -2.6%, GRID -2.1%, COPX -4.3%, REMX -2.8%. And the factor damage is systemic — MTUM 1m z=-2.6, SPHB/SPLV -5.4% on the day and at the 6th percentile, IWF/IWD at the 8th, ARKK -17.7% and IPO -10.5% on the month. Crypto remains the margin-call canary: MSTR -8.1% and -46.9% in a month at the 0th percentile, COIN -37.8%, IBIT -26.5%, even with BTC +1.8% to 60,802 today.

The offset is real and it is not defensive junk — it is earnings-visible cash flow. XLV +3.0% with relative strength +8.9% 1m, IBB +5.2% (97th percentile), XBI +6.6%, LLY +3.1%, IHI +1.7%. The consumer tape is the other uptrend: TGT +4.7% and +16.1% on the month, HD +2.2%, COST +2.2%, WMT +2.1%, MCD 1m z=2.38, NKE +5.9%, XRT +2.3% with XRT/SPY z=1.66. Housing is quietly turning — ITB +2.4% (+5.5% 1m), DHI +3.5%, XHB/SPY z=1.60, with the 30-year mortgage down 11bp on the month to 7.21. Breadth is the tell: RSP/SPY +1.0% with z=2.16 at the 90th percentile, IWM/SPY +1.0%, and IGV/SMH +7.9% in a single day, +6.5% on the month. The median stock is winning; the index is a cap-weighted hostage.

Macro is still a real-rate squeeze wearing a disinflation mask. The 10-year real yield is 2.79% with acceleration z=0.69 and sits 22% above its 200-day, while 5y breakevens collapsed to 2.13% (-34bp on the month, z=-1.62) and 10y to 2.12% at the 0th percentile. The 3-month bill is 4.36% against effective funds at 3.88%; 3m10y has flattened 27bp in a month to 0.51 and 2s10s is 0.24 at the 7th percentile. Commodities are the demand evidence: DBC 1m z=-3.05, Brent -21.7%, gasoline -24.8%, copper -16.1% (z=-2.49), gold -11.1%, silver -23.5% — today's +2.4% WTI, +1.9% copper, +0.8% gold bounce is noise against that. Natural gas is the exception and the consumer tax: +10.5% to 3.673, +41.2% on the month, acceleration z=2.2, into UMich sentiment at 48. FX is where the stress lives: DXY flat at 103.77 but USDBRL +19.0% in a month with z=5.15 and acceleration z=4.47, EWZ -31.2% (z=-3.9), USDMXN at the 100th percentile, CEW -2.6%, AUDUSD z=-2.08. The one clean EM winner is the big oil importer: INDA +13.5% on the month, z=3.05, Sensex +12.7%.

good.text: Index-level panic bled off: VIX 28.29 versus yesterday's 34 print, VIX3M 26.29, risk regime -19 from -22 and credit & vol -57 from -66. SPX only -0.3% on a day semis fell 8%.
Breadth is the strongest thing on the screen: RSP/SPY +1.0% with 1m z=2.16 (90th percentile), IWM/SPY +1.0%, RUT +0.7%, DJT +1.7%, SPW turning up. This is rotation, not liquidation.
New leadership is health care: XLV +3.0% (rs +8.9% 1m, +12.4% 3m), IBB +5.2% at the 97th percentile, XBI +6.6%, LLY +3.1%, IHI +1.7% and turning up.
The consumer and housing complex is bid into the holidays: TGT +4.7% (+16.1% 1m), HD +2.2%, COST +2.2%, WMT +2.1%, XRT/SPY +2.8%, ITB +2.4% (+5.5% 1m), DHI +3.5%, XHB/SPY z=1.60.

Disinflation is now overwhelming: 5y breakevens 2.13% (-34bp 1m, 3rd percentile), 10y 2.12% at the 0th, gasoline -24.8% and Brent -21.7% on the month, 30y mortgage -11bp to 7.21. That is the Fed's permission slip.

The pace of credit deterioration is slowing even as levels stay bad: CCC acceleration z=-2.19, HY -0.69, BBB -0.78, and leveraged loans BKLN +0.8% on the month with acceleration z=0.93 — no funding seizure yet.

bad.text: Credit keeps widening at the wides: HY +9bp to 3.72 (97th percentile), IG 0.98 and BBB 1.22 both 100th percentile, CCC 14.05 (+366bp in 3m), HYG/IEF z=-1.04 and rolling over.

The vol curve is still inverted and the inversion is accelerating: VIX/VIX3M 1.0761 (79th percentile, turning up, acc z=0.37), VIX3M acc z=0.80. Falling SKEW (-5.9% 1m) says tail hedges are being monetized, not re-bought.

Semis are in outright liquidation and it is spreading to the AI power chain: SOXX -8.3%, SMH -7.3% (18.7% below 200d), MU -11.0%, AMD -8.9%, NVDA -26.3% 1m, GEV -4.8%, ETN -5.1%, COPX -4.3%; KOSPI -5.0% and TAIEX -3.2% overnight.

Momentum and leveraged beta are being unwound wholesale: MTUM 1m z=-2.6, SPHB/SPLV -5.4% on the day at the 6th percentile, ARKK -17.7% 1m, IPO -10.5%, MSTR -46.9% and at the 0th percentile, COIN -37.8%.

Policy is tightening in real terms while nominals rally: 10y real yield 2.79% (acc z=0.69, 22% above 200d), 3m bill 4.36% versus 3.88% effective funds, 3m10y flattened 27bp in a month to 0.51, 2s10s 0.24 at the 7th percentile.

EM FX is the transmission channel and Brazil is a dislocation: USDBRL +19.0% on the month (z=5.15, acc z=4.47), EWZ -31.2% (z=-3.9), USDMXN at the 100th percentile, CEW -2.6%, AUDUSD z=-2.08, AUD/JPY -4.5%.

trades.name: Health over silicon
trades.line: Long IBB vs short SMH: leadership change, not a bounce
trades.expr: Buy IBB (add XBI for beta) against an equal-dollar short in SMH. Equal notional, rebalance weekly.
trades.thesis: The market is swapping capex-cycle risk for cash-flow visibility. Health care has the best relative-strength profile in the digest (XLV rs +8.9% 1m, +12.4% 3m, up) while semis own the worst (SMH/SPY 1m z=-2.34). This is where the money leaving the AI complex is going, and that rotation usually runs for a quarter, not a week.
trades.trigger: IBB +5.2% and XBI +6.6% on the day with XLV +3.0%, versus SMH -7.3% (-19.1% 1m, 18.7% below its 200-day), MU -11.0%, AMD -8.9%, NVDA -26.3% on the month. IGV/SMH +7.9% in one session confirms money is staying in tech-adjacent cash flow, not chips.
trades.stop: SMH reclaims its 200-day (roughly a 19% rally off here) or IBB's relative-strength trend rolls over; pair down 8%.
trades.target: +15% on the pair as SMH mean-reverts toward its 3m relative loss and IBB holds the 97th-percentile uptrend.

trades.name: The checkout aisle
trades.line: Long XRT + COST: the consumer tape is the last clean uptrend
trades.expr: Buy XRT, overweight with a COST position; fund by trimming high-beta growth exposure.
trades.thesis: Disinflation at the pump plus a labor market with claims at 189k is a real-income tailwind for the mass-market consumer right as positioning has abandoned the group. Retail relative strength is accelerating into the holiday print.
trades.trigger: XRT +2.3% with XRT/SPY +2.8% on the day (1m z=1.66, turning up), TGT +4.7% and +16.1% on the month at the 100th percentile, COST +2.2% and +12.0% 1m, WMT +2.1%, HD +2.2%, MCD 1m z=2.38. Gasoline -24.8% on the month.
trades.stop: Claims break back above 210k or XRT/SPY loses its turning-up state; position -6%.
trades.target: +10% as holiday comps confirm and the group re-rates off a 74th-percentile base.

trades.name: Molecule divergence
trades.line: Long natgas vs short Brent: winter bid against demand bust
trades.expr: Long front natural gas futures (or UNG-equivalent) against an equal-dollar short in Brent futures.
trades.thesis: One energy curve is pricing a weather/power squeeze, the other a global demand shock. Both are right, and the spread is the cleanest way to own commodity upside without owning the growth risk that crushed crude.
trades.trigger: Natgas +10.5% to 3.673 on the day, +41.2% on the month with acceleration z=2.2 and still only the 23rd percentile of the year, versus Brent -0.8% to 90.71 and -21.7% on the month (z=-2.19, acc -2.13), gasoline -24.8%, DBC z=-3.05.
trades.stop: Natgas loses 3.20 on a warm-weather shift or Brent reclaims 100 on a supply event; pair -12%.

trades.name: Own the belly, not the tail
trades.line: Long IEF vs short TLT: belly rally, long-end term premium
trades.expr: Long IEF against a 0.6x dollar short in TLT — duration-light, curve-flattening expression.
trades.thesis: Collapsing breakevens and a demand shock argue for cuts to be priced in the 2-5y, while the 30y stays hostage to supply and term premium. You want the policy-sensitive belly, not the long bond.
trades.trigger: 5y -21bp on the week to 4.69 versus 30y -16bp to 5.30 and +1bp today; 5y breakevens -34bp on the month to 2.13 (z=-1.62), 10y breakevens at the 0th percentile; 2s10s 0.24 at the 7th percentile and 3m10y -27bp on the month.
trades.stop: 2s10s steepens through 50bp or 10y breakevens reclaim 2.30 (reflation restart); pair -3%.
trades.target: +5% on the pair as the belly leads a cutting cycle being priced.

trades.name: Importer over exporter
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWT: cheap oil beats the chip cycle
trades.expr: Long INDA against an equal-dollar short in EWT.
trades.thesis: The commodity bust is a straight terms-of-trade transfer to India while Taiwan and Korea carry the semiconductor downcycle. This is the only EM pair where both legs are being driven by the same macro force in opposite directions.
trades.trigger: INDA +13.5% on the month with 1m z=3.05 and acceleration z=2.66 (Sensex +12.7%), versus EWT -19.4% on the month (z=-2.95), TAIEX -3.2% and KOSPI -5.0% overnight, Brent -21.7% and USDINR -2.2% on the month.
trades.stop: SMH makes a durable low and semis lead a tape-wide rally, or INDA's acceleration flips negative; pair -9%.

trades.name: Sell the levered crypto bounce
trades.line: Short MSTR into the bitcoin bid: forced-seller math
trades.expr: Short MSTR outright, or buy 1-3 month puts; size small, this is a high-vol tail trade.
trades.thesis: MSTR is the levered expression of a bitcoin drawdown that is still in progress. Its equity is down far more than its NAV asset, which tells you the financing premium is unwinding, not just the coin price. Today's crypto bounce is the exit.
trades.trigger: BTC +1.8% to 60,802 but still -24.8% on the month; MSTR -8.1% on the day, -46.9% on the month, 1m z=-1.63, 0th percentile of the year and 41% below its 200-day; COIN -5.9%, IBIT -2.5% and -26.5% 1m.
trades.stop: BTC reclaims 72,000 and MSTR closes above its 50-day; short -22%.

trades.name: Quality inside credit
trades.line: Short HYG vs long LQD: HY out 34bp, IG out 7bp
trades.expr: Short HYG against an equal-dollar long in LQD; a cheap, carry-light hedge on the rest of the book.
trades.thesis: Credit is widening but not uniformly — the stress is concentrated in the low-quality tail. Owning IG against HY captures that dispersion without paying for outright duration or an equity hedge that decays.
trades.trigger: HY OAS +9bp to 3.72 and +34bp on the month (z=1.14) versus IG +1bp to 0.98 and +7bp on the month; CCC 14.05 and +366bp in three months; HYG -0.3% on the month against LQD +0.3%; HYG/IEF 1m z=-1.04 and rolling over.
trades.stop: HY OAS tightens back below 3.40 with VIX under 20; pair -3%.
trades.target: +5% on the pair if HY retests this year's wides while IG holds.
